contexts.text: Let the dry [land] appear ().
The external man himself is called the dry [land], and presently the land.
God called the dry [land] earth ().
I will shake the heavens and the earth, and the sea and the dry [land] (). Here a new Church is treated of.

Of all that was in the dry [land] () = those in whom there was no longer anything of such life... It is dry where there is no water, that is, where there is no longer anything spiritual, still less celestial. The persuasion of falsity extinguishes and as it were suffocates everything spiritual and celestial... They who have once formed opinions... inhere in them so obstinately, that they do not want to hear anything contrary to them; thus they never suffer themselves to be instructed, even if the truth is set before their eyes. This is still more the case when they cultivate a false opinion from a kind of sanctity; for such persons reject all truth, and that which they admit they pervert, and thus infuse with phantasies. These are they who are here signified by the dry [land], on which there is neither water nor grass; as in Ezekiel: I will make the rivers dry [land]... (). To make the rivers dry [land] = that there is no longer anything spiritual. And in Jeremiah: Your land is become dry (). Dry = land which is desolated and wasted, so that there is no longer anything of truth and good.

Thou shalt pour upon the dry [land] () = immission into the Natural... The dry [land] = the Natural. Dry is used to express a dry place, and also the land, and the land of Egypt = the natural mind, which is in falsity, thus the Natural; and still more so the dry [land].

The Sons of Israel shall come into the midst of the sea in the dry () = that those who are of the Spiritual Church may pass through safely and without the influx of falsity... In the dry = safely and without the influx of falsity; for the waters of that sea = falsities from evil; hence dry = devoid of falsity. Illustrated. AC 8205. AC 8234.
But when waters = truths, drying up arefactio-signifies a state of no truth, or devoid of truth. Illustrated.

Where, however, dry, or drying up is said in the Word of other things, as of trees, herbs, the harvest, or of bones, the contrary is signified thereby. The land itself is also called dry relatively to the sea, and then dry is predicated of good, and the sea, of truth.

Without such a change of the states, the good of celestial love would become as it were dry... This is signified by the Sons of Israel calling the manna dry food, and vile food, when the quails were no longer given; as in Moses... Our soul is dry, there is not anything which our eyes [may look to] but to manna ().
In the Spiritual World, they who are in the internals of the Church, appear upon the dry, and they who are in its externals as it were in the seas.
It here treats of the illumination of the gentiles. Their ignorance of truth and good is signified by the wilderness and the dry place ().
The desolation of all truth is signified by I will give thee into the dryness of the rock (); the rock = truth; and dryness, its desolation.
The sea and the dry [land] () = all the exterior things of the Church.
Dry bones () = those with whom there is not anything of spiritual life. AE 419:3.
A land of dryness () = the Church where there is 110 good; and a land of thirst, where there is no truth. AE 727:3. AE 730:10.
That they were averse to spiritual things, is signified by Our soul is dry...
To pour floods upon the dry [land] () = to give intelligence to those who, from good, have a longing for truth.
I will make the rivers dry [land] () = that there is no longer any Knowledge and apperception of truth.

It here treats of the establishment of the Church by the Lord; and that then there will be intelligence through Divine truth spiritual with those with whom before there was not any, is signified by the dry place shall be for a pool ().
The Church devoid of good is signified by the wilderness, and a land of drought ()... Drought is said of the want of good, because it is caused by burning.
Our soul is dry = the life of faith and of the understanding lacking when there is not natural nourishment at the same time.
